name: Hu Chun
current_role: Controlling shareholder and actual controller, Suzhou Electrical Apparatus Science Academy Co. (EETI, SZSE: 300215); no longer a director since June 2025
profile: Hu Chun (b. 1978) is the son of Hu Delin, who led the privatisation of the Suzhou Electrical Apparatus Science Research Institute (founded 1965, restructured 2000) into EETI, one of China's largest third-party testing labs for high/low-voltage electrical, wind, solar and EV-charging equipment. He was chairman in 2019-21 and 2022-23 and remains its controlling shareholder.
interesting_fact: EETI runs national testing centres for electrical products, smart-grid switchgear and explosion-proof equipment, and is an accredited IECEx and IECEE-CB lab, making it a key gatekeeper for China's grid and renewable-equipment makers.
deep_cut_fact: Long before becoming chairman in November 2019, he served as a director and deputy general manager of the testing institute from 2002 to 2016. In July 2026 the company disclosed he had become a Canadian citizen.
notes: Company site is EETI (eeti.cn); the company is chaired by Yuan Lei since July 2025. Board governance disputes in 2022-23 between Hu Chun and his father Hu Delin were widely reported, so avoid that topic. No personal public channels found; route via company board secretary/IR (SZSE 300215).

name: Wen Kaifu
current_role: Founder and former controlling shareholder of Holitech Technology (合力泰, SZSE: 002217); no current executive role found
profile: Wen Kaifu built Holitech, a Shandong-based maker of touch screens, LCD modules and other display components for smartphones. In 2018 he handed control (via a voting-rights proxy and share transfers) to the state-owned Fujian Electronics & Information Group, which now controls the company.
interesting_fact: Holitech grew into one of China's larger suppliers of touch-display modules for smartphone brands before Fujian Electronics & Information Group took control around 2018.
notes: Not a good outreach target: in June 2026 Holitech disclosed a regulator's preliminary penalty notice naming the company and Wen Kaifu over 2017-2021 financial misreporting, and reports say he faces a lifetime securities-market ban and his shares are judicially frozen (news.10jqka.com.cn/20260901/c679501996.shtml). No personal public channels found.

name: Sir Martyn Arbib
current_role: Founder of Perpetual (now Invesco); philanthropist via the Arbib Foundation
profile: Sir Martyn Arbib (b. 1939, Hendon) founded fund manager Perpetual in 1973 in a small office on Hart Street, Henley-on-Thames, and sold it to AMVESCAP in 2001 for over £1bn; it became Invesco Perpetual. He left Perpetual's board in 2015 and focuses on philanthropy through the Arbib Foundation (est. 1987), which sponsors schools in Slough including Langley Academy.
interesting_fact: He was knighted in 2003 for services to charity, especially education; his foundation sponsors academies in Slough including The Langley Academy.
deep_cut_fact: His 1994 backing of Henley's River and Rowing Museum was what allowed the founders to commission architect David Chipperfield for the building, which opened in 1998 (and later won a Royal Fine Art Commission Building of the Year award).
notes: Very private, now in his late 80s; no personal website or social accounts found. Alive status assumed (no death notice found). The River and Rowing Museum closed in September 2025, so avoid framing it as current. Best route is likely via the Arbib Foundation (registered charity) or Langley Academy.

name: Liao Wen
current_role: Pre-IPO shareholder of Hi-Target Navigation Tech (中海达, SZSE: 300177); no executive role found
profile: Liao Wen appears on the Hurun list jointly with Liao Dinghai, founder, chairman and controlling shareholder of Guangzhou-based Hi-Target, a maker of high-precision GNSS receivers, CORS stations, total stations, 3D laser scanners and drones. Liao Wen was named as a shareholder in Hi-Target's 2011 IPO lock-up undertakings; the exact relationship to Liao Dinghai is not stated in the filings found.
interesting_fact: Hi-Target, founded in Guangzhou in 1999, is one of China's main makers of BeiDou/GNSS high-precision surveying equipment.
notes: Low public profile; the wealth figure is shared with Liao Dinghai, the public face of the company. Any outreach is better aimed at Liao Dinghai via Hi-Target's board secretary/IR. Relationship between Liao Wen and Liao Dinghai not confirmed.

name: Zhang Shiquan
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Zhejiang Shibao Co. (浙江世宝, SZSE: 002703 / HKEX: 1057)
profile: Zhang Shiquan (b. c.1950) co-founded Zhejiang Shibao in Yiwu in 1993 and, with family members, controls it. Shibao designs and makes automotive steering gears and steering-system components, with subsidiaries such as Siping Steering Gear and Wuhu Sterling Steering Systems. He was CEO until December 2017 and remains chairman.
interesting_fact: Shibao is dual-listed in Hong Kong and Shenzhen and is one of China's main independent steering-system suppliers, now developing electric power steering for new-energy and intelligent vehicles.
deep_cut_fact: He served as Shibao's chief executive for over 24 years, from its founding in June 1993 until December 2017, before handing the CEO job on while staying chairman.
notes: Low media profile; the controlling group includes several Zhang family members. Best route is via the company's board secretary / IR (HKEX 1057 filings list company secretary contacts).

name: Tom Singh
current_role: Founder of New Look (retired from board 2019); private investor and non-executive director (e.g. Ace Turtle, India)
profile: Punjab-born Tom Singh OBE (b. 1949), who came to England as a baby, founded high-street fashion chain New Look in Taunton in 1969 and built it into one of the UK's biggest fashion retailers. He retired from the New Look board in 2019 after its debt restructuring and now invests in retail and consumer businesses, including Castore and Indian omnichannel firm Ace Turtle.
interesting_fact: He started New Look in 1969 with a £5,000 loan from his parents, after earlier selling goods on a market stall in Wellington, Somerset.
deep_cut_fact: He studied international politics and geography at the University of Wales, Aberystwyth, and his younger brother is the science writer and broadcaster Simon Singh (author of Fermat's Last Theorem).
notes: Low-profile since retiring in 2019; no personal website or social accounts found. Was a partner at Magenta Partners and joined Ace Turtle's board in 2021; those firms may be a route. Avoid New Look's later financial troubles as a topic.

name: Xu Liping
current_role: Co-owner (30%) of Donly Holding Group, controlling shareholder of Ningbo Donly Co. (宁波东力, SZSE: 002164); direct 3.81% shareholder
profile: Xu Liping and her husband Song Jilong (Donly chairman since 2006) are the controlling family behind Ningbo Donly, whose Donly Transmission subsidiary (founded 1993) makes industrial gear reducers, motors, gearboxes, couplings and brakes. She holds 30% of the Donly Holding parent and a direct stake in the listed company, but is not an executive.
interesting_fact: Donly's transmission business, started in Ningbo in 1993, supplies heavy-duty gearboxes and reducers used in steel, mining, cement and port equipment.
notes: Not a public-facing executive; her husband Song Jilong is the company's chairman and public face, so outreach is best directed at him via the securities department (zq@donly.com, per the 2024 annual report).

name: Luo Ruifa
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Shenzhen Genvict Technologies (金溢科技, SZSE: 002869)
profile: Luo Ruifa (b. 1976), a senior engineer in transport information engineering, co-founded Shenzhen-based Genvict in 2004. It became a leading maker of ETC (electronic toll collection) on-board units, with cumulative OBU sales passing 100 million around China's 2019-20 removal of provincial toll stations. He now steers it toward vehicle-road coordination (V2X), smart highways and transport-energy integration.
interesting_fact: Genvict built its first-generation ETC product in 2004, deployed in Guangdong, and helped draft China's national ETC standards; its OBU sales topped 100 million units during the 2019-20 nationwide toll-booth removal programme.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Genvict he was a department manager at Guangzhou telecom-equipment firm Etes Communication; he is now pursuing a PhD in transportation at Tongji University and chairs the Shenzhen Smart Transportation Industry Promotion Association.
notes: Strong podcast fit: Genvict's 2025 strategy pivots to 'transport-energy integration' (digital energy, connected transport). He holds many industry-association roles in Shenzhen, so is relatively accessible via IR/board office.

name: Guo Song
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, UROVO Technology (优博讯, SZSE: 300531)
profile: Guo Song (b. 1965, Singaporean national) leads Shenzhen-based UROVO, a maker of rugged handheld mobile computers, PDAs, barcode scanners and smart POS terminals for logistics, retail and payments. He joined as deputy GM in 2006, rose to chairman and GM, and is one of the company's actual controllers via its Hong Kong holding company.
interesting_fact: UROVO's handheld data terminals are widely used by China's courier and logistics companies for parcel scanning; it is one of the country's main mobile-intelligent-terminal suppliers.
deep_cut_fact: He studied information engineering at Huazhong University of Science and Technology and took a master's in electronic engineering at the National University of Singapore; he was named a 2013 innovation figure of China's logistics technology equipment industry.

public_contacts.value: info@urovo.com (company securities/IR contact per 2025 annual report)

notes: Avoid referencing the March 2025 death of former vice-chair and co-controller Liu Dan. Route via the board secretary (Liu Zhen) at the published IR address.

name: Yang Guimo
current_role: Founder and former actual controller of Shandong Weida Machinery (山东威达, SZSE: 002026); left the board Feb 2025
profile: Yang Guimo (b. c.1949) built Weihai-based Shandong Weida, a major maker of drill chucks, saw blades and precision power-tool parts that has diversified into energy-storage lithium battery packs and EV battery-swap stations. In July 2024 he transferred control to his daughter Yang Mingyan, now chair and GM, and stepped off the board at the February 2025 term end.
interesting_fact: A power-tool-accessories manufacturer, Weida now also builds energy-storage battery packs and battery-swap stations for new-energy vehicles.
deep_cut_fact: The 2024 handover was structured as a family succession: control of Weida Group passed from Yang Guimo to his daughter Yang Mingyan, who started as a staff member at Shandong Weida Machine Tool Group before rising to chair.
notes: Now retired from the board (aged ~76). For a podcast on energy, his daughter Yang Mingyan (chair) is the more relevant guest given Weida's battery-swap and storage business. Hurun listing shared with Yang Mingyan.

name: Zhu Zheng
current_role: Private investor; formerly a 6.34% individual shareholder of Jiangsu Shagang Co. (沙钢股份, SZSE: 002075)
profile: Zhu Zheng appeared on Hurun China 2015-2018 on the strength of a 140 million-share (6.34%) stake in Jiangsu Shagang Co., the listed steel arm of the Shagang group, as shown in its 2016 annual report. He was an investor rather than an executive, and he no longer appears among the top shareholders in the 2025 report.
notes: Financial investor with no public profile, executive role or published contacts; Shagang itself is controlled by Shen Wenrong's Jiangsu Shagang Group. Low priority for outreach. Source: http://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2017-03-28/1203211716.PDF

name: Deng Zichang
current_role: Co-founder and former chairman/GM of Shenzhen Changfang Semiconductor Lighting (长方集团, SZSE: 300301); no current role found
profile: Deng Zichang (b. May 1967) co-founded Shenzhen Changfang with his brothers Deng Zihua, Deng Ziquan and Deng Zixian, building it into an LED packaging and lighting maker that listed on ChiNext in 2012. He was chairman and GM in the early 2010s; the family later gave up control of the company.
interesting_fact: Changfang was a family affair: four Deng brothers held the chairman and deputy-GM posts when it listed in 2012.
deep_cut_fact: Before LEDs he ran a string of small businesses: motorcycle repair in Luohu, Shenzhen, car trading at the Futian stadium, a preserved-fruit (liangguo) trade at a Puning overseas-Chinese farm, and IT sales in Huaqiangbei.
notes: No longer associated with the company's management; Changfang (now 'ST Changfang') IR email ir@cfled.com is not a route to him. No personal public channels found.

name: Li Yuhu
current_role: Executive Director and GM, Xinjiang Maiquer Group (parent of Maiquer Group Co., SZSE: 002719); co-actual controller
profile: Li Yuhu heads the family that controls Xinjiang-based Maiquer Group, a dairy and bakery/food company listed in Shenzhen. He and his wife Wang Cuixian, with sons Li Yong (chairman) and Li Gang (GM), are its ultimate controllers; he is executive director and GM of the parent, Xinjiang Maiquer Group.
interesting_fact: Maiquer is one of Xinjiang's best-known home-grown food brands, combining dairy (milk) with bakery and festive foods such as mooncakes.
notes: Day-to-day leadership has passed to his sons; the listed company carries 'ST' status, so avoid financial topics. Route via the board office (bod@maiquer.com).
